Search: SelectorStrategy|ResolveSelector|NotSupportedExceptionRead: UiaHelper.csSearch: SelectorStrategy|new Selector\(|ParseSelector|--strategyRead (2 completed)2 tasks done**Investigation summary:** Four call sites parse `--strategy`/`--scopeStrategy` via raw `Enum.TryParse<SelectorStrategy>` (`WaitForElement` L738, `ParseSelectorArgs` L1320 — shared by `find-first`/`find-all`, `ResolveFindScope`'s `--scopeStrategy` L1371, `ResolveElement` L1421 — shared by `click`/`type`/`get-text`/`send-keys`/`submit-chat-message`). All accept `NameRegex`/`ControlTypeIndex`/`Coordinates` today since `Enum.TryParse` only checks the enum has a matching name, not whether `UiaHelper` implements it.

**Proposed Pre-Build Decomposition (Phase 16):**

**Part A — Central helper:** Add a single static helper (e.g. `UiaHelper.TryParseImplementedSelectorStrategy(string text, out SelectorStrategy strategy, out string error)`) that wraps `Enum.TryParse` and additionally rejects `NameRegex`/`ControlTypeIndex`/`Coordinates` explicitly, returning a clean error message ("`--strategy` must be one of the implemented values: Name, AutomationId.") — this is the one place the "implemented" set is defined, so `ResolveSelector`/`ResolveSelectorAll`'s `NotSupportedException` becomes unreachable from any CLI path.

**Part B — Replace all 4 call sites** in `Program.cs` (`WaitForElement`, `ParseSelectorArgs`, `ResolveFindScope`'s scope-strategy check, `ResolveElement`) to call this helper instead of raw `Enum.TryParse`, each returning/writing `invalid-argument` with the new message on failure — same error code already used, just now reachable for these three strategies too.

**Part C — Docs:** Update `docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md` wherever `--strategy` is documented to note only `Name`/`AutomationId` are currently accepted (reject others with `invalid-argument`), and mark this finding resolved in `docs/KNOWN_OPEN_FINDINGS.md` after confirmation.

Note: I will *not* remove the `NotSupportedException` fallback in `UiaHelper.ResolveSelector`/`ResolveSelectorAll` — it stays as defense-in-depth for any future internal caller, just becomes unreachable via the CLI once Part A/B are in place.
